criteria_note: E2 is judged by the defect's mechanism: it passes when the racing window contains the application's database statements and the wrong outcome is database state reachable through the public API; it fails when the race is between in-process coroutines with no statement in the window.

screened.subject: fix(queue): a timed-out postgres dequeue must take its buffered job
read: parent's Worker (start, upkeep, process, _process, _check_burst) and docstring
screened.note: E2: the racing window is a claim transaction (UPDATE ... SET status='active') committed on behalf of a waiter whose dequeue_timeout expired; the wrong outcome is a job left 'active' in the database. E3: Postgres queue, poll mode, one-connection pool (0.26.x needs only one connection per queue). E4: Worker docstring (burst, dequeue_timeout), maintainers' test added by the fix (test_dequeue_takes_job_buffered_while_waiting) and existing burst tests. E5: job statuses in the final state plus the worker's handled list. E6: pinned public tree; fix diff and the dequeue/worker path reviewed.

screened.subject: fix: deadlock in Queue.listen from asyncio.wait_for swallowed cancellation
screened.note: A CPython asyncio defect (bpo-42130, before 3.12): wait_for loses a cancellation. Pure in-process logic. (E3 would also fail: the runner is CPython 3.12.)

screened.subject: fix: make init_db advisory lock transaction-scoped
read: docs/ and README grep (no init_db or migration text)
screened.note: E2: init_db's session-level pg_try_advisory_lock outlives init_db on the pooled connection, so another queue's init_db skips its migrations; database-mediated, through connect(). E4 is the weakest of the saq cases: no regression test in the fix; the contract is the PostgresQueue docstring (versions_table 'SAQ will use to maintain migrations', jobs_table, stats_table as constructor arguments) plus the maintainers' own statement of the defect in the commit message. Judged PASS on the docstring; recorded as weak. E5: the second queue's enqueue results and the final tables.

screened.subject: fix: KeyError on concurrent same-key job attempts in job_task_contexts
screened.note: The race is between two coroutines' finally blocks over the Worker's in-memory job_task_contexts dict (keyed by Job.key); no database statement is in the racing window. Pure in-process logic.

screened.subject: fix: Do wait to cancel task in case of timeout
screened.note: On a job timeout the worker didn't await the task's cancellation: asyncio task lifecycle, in-process.

screened.subject: fix: Avoid race in setting task status b/w process and abort
screened.note: Database-mediated (Queue.abort writes 'aborting'; the worker's abort poller reads it; both paths write the final status) and under the seam. But no documented contract decides it: Job.abort is documented as 'Tries to abort the job.', the fix has no test, and the overwrite needs a handler that returns normally after cancellation, which no doc addresses.

screened.subject: fix: Avoid race in stop()
screened.note: Re-entrant Worker.stop() (signal handler and finally) cancelling tasks and running shutdown hooks twice: in-process.

screened.subject: fix: ensure there's no race condition in between dequeue and processing for sweeper
screened.note: saq before v0.25.0 (93775ff 'refactor!: remove pg locks for stability', first in v0.25.0) holds a dedicated dequeue connection (PostgresQueue._get_dequeue_conn: pool.getconn() kept for the queue's life, carrying the job advisory locks) while every other call uses pool.connection(): one queue needs two concurrent connections. The seam gives each actor exactly one stepped connection and refuses a second; two connections per actor would be an engine extension. Unsupported: E3 fails.
